newsitem.title: USA: PEPCO sees 341 MW Md. coal unit up Friday.
newsitem.headline: PEPCO sees 341 MW Md. coal unit up Friday.

text.p: Potomac Electric Power Co (PEPCO) said Thursday the 341 megawatt (MW) unit 1 at its Chalk Point generating facility would resume operation Friday.
The coal-fired unit was shut last weekend to correct a boiler tube leak.
Repair of a condenser water box leak at the oil-fired 672 MW Chalk Point unit 3 was completed, PEPCO said.
"Unit 3 has been repaired, but is not needed today," said a company spokeswoman, adding Chalk Point 3 is fired up only to meet peak electricity demand.
The utility predicted it could meet today's electricity load on its system with Chalk Point 3, she said.
PEPCO is the operator and owner of the Chalk Point complex in Aquasco, Md. The facility has four units, whose installed capacity totals just above 2,000 MW.
Potomac Electric Power is headquartered in Washington DC.
